evidence.text: The adult human skeleton typically consists of 206 bones. Infants are born with approximately 270 bones, many of which fuse together during development. The skeleton is divided into the axial skeleton (80 bones) and the appendicular skeleton (126 bones).
evidence.snippet: The adult human skeleton typically consists of 206 bones, divided into axial (80) and appendicular (126) skeleton.

evidence.snippet: Medical science recognises 206 bones in the standard adult skeleton.

rationale.e1: Both sources confirm the human body contains bones
rationale.e2: Both sources confirm 206 as the standard adult count

evidence.snippet: Renewable sources generated 30.3% of all electricity globally in 2023, up from 28.7% in 2022.

_rule_tested: TOPIC vs FIGURE + STATE RULE (context-only → unresolved)
_trap: Evidence discusses the UK space industry extensively but never mentions any revenue figure. For e2, all evidence should map as 'context' (topic without figure), forcing 'unresolved' via STATE RULE.
normalised_claim: The UK space industry generates £16.4 billion in annual revenue

elements.description: The UK has a space industry that generates revenue
The annual revenue of the UK space industry is £16.4 billion

evidence.title: UK Space Agency Annual Review
evidence.text: The UK Space Agency supports a growing domestic space sector, with investments across satellite technology, launch capability, and space science. The agency awarded over £150 million in grants during 2023-24 to support commercial space ventures and research institutions.
evidence.snippet: The UK Space Agency supports a growing space sector with investments in satellite technology, launch capability, and space science.

evidence.title: Britain's space sector continues to expand
evidence.text: The UK's space industry continues to expand, attracting international investment and creating high-skilled jobs across the country. New spaceport developments in Scotland and Cornwall signal growing ambitions in the launch market.
evidence.snippet: The UK space industry continues to expand, attracting international investment and creating high-skilled jobs.

evidence.title: Space sector workforce and capabilities
evidence.text: Industry leaders describe the UK space sector as one of the fastest-growing in Europe, with world-leading capabilities in small satellite manufacturing, Earth observation, and telecommunications. The sector employs over 47,000 people directly.
evidence.snippet: Industry leaders describe the UK space sector as one of the fastest-growing in Europe, employing over 47,000 people.

rationale.e1: Multiple sources confirm the UK has a space industry (grants, jobs, investment) — revenue generation is implied
rationale.e2: No source mentions £16.4 billion or ANY revenue figure. All evidence discusses the topic (growing, investing, employing) without the specific statistic. TOPIC vs FIGURE rule: evidence about a topic without the figure is 'context'. STATE RULE: context-only refs → unresolved

_rule_tested: CROSS-ELEMENT — single evidence item informing multiple elements differently
_trap: One evidence item (NASA) contains data relevant to BOTH elements but with different relationships — height is correct (supports), location is wrong (challenges). Model must apply CROSS-ELEMENT rule.
normalised_claim: Mount Kilimanjaro is 5,895 metres tall and is located in Kenya

elements.description: Mount Kilimanjaro is 5,895 metres tall
Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Kenya

evidence.title: Mount Kilimanjaro - Geographic Survey
evidence.text: Mount Kilimanjaro, located in northeastern Tanzania near the Kenyan border, stands at 5,895 metres above sea level. It is the highest peak in Africa and the tallest freestanding mountain in the world. The mountain lies within Kilimanjaro National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
evidence.snippet: Mount Kilimanjaro, in northeastern Tanzania near the Kenyan border, stands at 5,895 metres. It is the highest peak in Africa.

evidence.title: Climbing Kilimanjaro: Routes and Logistics
evidence.text: All official climbing routes to the summit of Kilimanjaro begin in Tanzania, as the mountain is entirely within Tanzanian territory. Climbers typically fly into Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO), located between Moshi and Arusha in Tanzania.
evidence.snippet: All climbing routes begin in Tanzania, as Kilimanjaro is entirely within Tanzanian territory.

rationale.e1: NatGeo confirms height of 5,895 metres — exact match
rationale.e2: Both sources state Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, not Kenya. NatGeo says 'near the Kenyan border' but explicitly 'in Tanzania'. Alpine Club says 'entirely within Tanzanian territory'. Same evidence item (ev-230) supports e1 and challenges e2 — CROSS-ELEMENT rule

_rule_tested: PRECISION — approximate leniency (near-miss that SHOULD be supported)
_trap: Evidence says 55-65% and 57-60%, claim says 'approximately 60%'. Model must apply PRECISION rule — round/approximate figures treat close matches as supporting, not challenging.
normalised_claim: Approximately 60% of the adult human body is composed of water

elements.description: The adult human body contains a significant proportion of water
The proportion is approximately 60%

evidence.title: Human Body Composition - Physiology Textbook
evidence.text: Water makes up approximately 55-65% of total body weight in adults, varying by age, sex, and body composition. The commonly cited figure of 60% represents an average for adult males. Women typically have a lower percentage (50-55%) due to higher average body fat, which contains less water than lean tissue.
evidence.snippet: Water makes up approximately 55-65% of adult body weight. The commonly cited figure of 60% represents an average for adult males.

evidence.title: Water and the Human Body
evidence.text: The average adult body is about 57-60% water by weight according to multiple physiological studies. This proportion decreases with age, as older adults tend to have lower total body water percentages.
evidence.snippet: The average adult body is about 57-60% water by weight according to multiple physiological studies.

rationale.e1: Both sources confirm the human body contains substantial water
rationale.e2: Both sources cite ranges (55-65%, 57-60%) that encompass 60%. The textbook explicitly confirms '60% represents an average'. PRECISION rule: 'approximately 60%' with evidence in the 57-65% range is a match, not a challenge

_trap: Commentary says 'one of the most capable military powers' and analysis says 'increasing' — sounds supportive. But primary data says 2.3% GDP, well below the claimed 3%. Commentary is 'context' under DATA PROVENANCE rule.
normalised_claim: UK defence spending exceeded 3% of GDP in 2024

elements.description: The UK allocates spending to defence
UK defence spending exceeded 3% of GDP in 2024

evidence.title: UK Defence Expenditure 2023-24
evidence.text: UK defence expenditure was 2.3% of GDP in 2023-24, above the NATO minimum commitment of 2% but below the government's stated aspiration of reaching 2.5% of GDP. Total defence spending was approximately £54.2 billion.
evidence.snippet: UK defence expenditure was 2.3% of GDP in 2023-24, above the NATO 2% minimum but below the 2.5% aspiration.

evidence.title: Britain's military standing in a changing world
evidence.text: Britain remains one of the most capable military powers in Europe, maintaining a nuclear deterrent capability, two aircraft carriers, and significant expeditionary capacity. Defence analysts regard the UK as NATO's most important European ally.
evidence.snippet: Britain remains one of the most capable military powers in Europe, with nuclear deterrent and significant expeditionary capacity.

evidence.title: Rising defence budgets across NATO
evidence.text: Defence spending has been increasing across NATO allies as geopolitical tensions rise. The UK government has announced a pathway to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with incremental annual increases planned. Several Eastern European nations have already exceeded 3%.
evidence.snippet: UK government announced a pathway to 2.5% of GDP by 2030. Several Eastern European nations have already exceeded 3%.

rationale.e1: Government data confirms £54.2 billion defence spending — the UK clearly allocates to defence
rationale.e2: Primary data says 2.3% of GDP, not 3%. Commentary about military capability (ev-251) is 'context' under DATA PROVENANCE — it discusses the topic without confirming the figure. Analysis about future plans (ev-252) is also 'context' — aspirations to reach 2.5% by 2030 actually reinforces that current spending is below 3%

_rule_tested: TOPIC vs FIGURE — evidence discusses topic extensively but never cites the claimed figure
_trap: Evidence strongly establishes that plastic pollution harms marine mammals, making e1 clearly supported. But NO source cites 100,000 or any figure for annual deaths — model must recognise the figure is unaddressed.
normalised_claim: Plastic pollution kills approximately 100,000 marine mammals every year

elements.description: Plastic pollution causes death in marine mammals
Approximately 100,000 marine mammals are killed by plastic pollution per year

evidence.title: Marine Debris and Plastic Pollution
evidence.text: Marine plastic debris has been found in the digestive systems of over 700 marine species, including numerous marine mammal species such as whales, dolphins, and seals. Entanglement in abandoned fishing gear and ingestion of microplastics are the primary pathways of harm, frequently causing injury, starvation, and death.
evidence.snippet: Marine plastic has been found in over 700 species. Entanglement and ingestion frequently cause injury, starvation, and death in marine mammals.

evidence.title: UNEP: Plastic pollution threatens ocean ecosystems
evidence.text: A UNEP report described plastic pollution as one of the greatest threats to ocean ecosystems, with over 11 million tonnes of plastic waste entering the oceans each year. The report calls for urgent international action to reduce plastic production and improve waste management systems globally.
evidence.snippet: UNEP described plastic pollution as one of the greatest threats to ocean ecosystems, with 11 million tonnes entering oceans annually.

rationale.e1: Science.org confirms plastic causes 'injury, starvation, and death' in marine mammals — directly supports
rationale.e2: Neither source mentions 100,000 or ANY figure for annual marine mammal deaths. TOPIC vs FIGURE rule: evidence about the topic (plastic harms marine life) without the figure (100,000 per year) should be mapped as 'context', not 'supports'. STATE RULE: context-only → unresolved

_trap: Regional data (North America 87%, South Korea 97%) exceeds 85%. But GLOBAL figure is 68%. Model must apply SCOPE CHECK to reject regional data for a global claim, AND recognise 68% ≠ 85% via PRECISION rule.
normalised_claim: Global smartphone penetration reached 85% in 2024

elements.description: Smartphones are widely used across the world
Global smartphone penetration reached 85% in 2024

evidence.title: GSMA Mobile Economy Report 2024
evidence.text: Global smartphone adoption stood at 68% of the world's population as of mid-2024, with significant regional variation. Sub-Saharan Africa (28%) and South Asia (44%) remain below the global average, while smartphone penetration in North America reached 87% and in Western Europe 84%.
evidence.snippet: Global smartphone adoption was 68% as of mid-2024. North America reached 87%, Western Europe 84%, while Sub-Saharan Africa was at 28%.

evidence.title: Asia leads smartphone adoption
evidence.text: South Korea leads global smartphone penetration at 97%, followed by the UAE at 96% and several other developed Asian markets above 90%. Analysts attribute this to high disposable income, advanced 5G infrastructure, and strong digital payment ecosystems.
evidence.snippet: South Korea leads smartphone penetration at 97%, followed by UAE at 96%, with several Asian markets above 90%.

rationale.e1: GSMA confirms widespread global adoption (68%), with multiple regions showing high penetration — smartphones are widely used
rationale.e2: GSMA reports GLOBAL penetration at 68%, not 85%. Regional figures (North America 87%, South Korea 97%) are higher but SCOPE CHECK prohibits using country/regional data for a global claim. 68% vs 85% is a clear mismatch (PRECISION: 17 percentage points apart)
